reviews.text: I was shocked to hear that an acquaintance of mine received a bill for 270,000 yen after hospitalizing their child for 2-3 days. I had heard stories of exorbitant bills many times before, but I tried not to pry into that family's affairs. The child ultimately passed away on the day of discharge, but they were forced to buy an oxygen chamber upon discharge, and they were paying exorbitant bills right up to the very end. I had heard rumors, but I didn't think it was that bad. I'm sure there are children who have been saved by this hospital, but the bills are so outrageous that it seems like they're from a scam, so you should be prepared for that.

This is my first review.

I wanted to share this with everyone so much that I'm writing this review for the first time.

I took my beloved cat, who has a serious chronic illness, to this hospital.

She had been in and out of the hospital for a long time, but we finally found a medication that worked, and for the past six months she had been stable and healthy.

Due to work, my base of operations changed, and I had to start searching for a hospital from scratch. I found a trustworthy specialist at a different hospital. At that time, I was relieved when they said her condition had improved since the last examination.

However, the hospital that had prescribed the medication didn't have it in stock, and I was told to go to another hospital to pick it up, so I went to this hospital.

I was told that it was difficult to get a prescription for medication only, so I had to have a consultation before getting the prescription.

I wish they had prescribed the medication as written on the prescription, but instead, they prescribed the wrong amount, and my cat's condition suddenly worsened.

When I noticed that the dosage was wrong and mentioned it, their statements changed two or three times, sometimes saying the prescription was correct, and sometimes saying it was wrong. At that point, I realized I had come to a bad hospital.

After taking the medication prescribed here, my cat vomited (she had never vomited before). I immediately took her to this hospital for a blood test, but they said there was nothing wrong.

Since the blood test results were normal, I had to pay for the follow-up visit myself (they eventually admitted that the medication dosage was incorrect).

However, she subsequently lost her appetite, and two days later, her condition suddenly worsened. She is now hospitalized in the ICU at another hospital.

I'm incredibly frustrated, thinking that this wouldn't have happened if the medication prescribed here hadn't been wrong.

This might sound like hindsight, but I had a feeling of distrust from my interaction with the doctor during the initial consultation, and I regret not taking that distrust more seriously.

I don't want any other cat to go through this.

I'm willing to pay for good medical care, but I received such a shoddy prescription, and the bill came to around 150,000 yen.

I paid a large sum of money only to have my beloved cat's healthy life taken away from me.

I looked at other websites as well, and it seemed like there were more negative reviews for this hospital than others.

Please choose a hospital carefully for your precious family member so you don't regret it. I cannot recommend this hospital.
The experience was excellent, the speed was very fast, and my kitten didn't experience any discomfort afterwards.

I had been a patient for many years, but I was deeply hurt by the inconsistent and unpleasant service I received.

I trusted this clinic and continued to visit, but recently, when I went in just to pick up my medication (without a consultation), there was a significant misunderstanding and a very disappointing incident.

My appointment was for the last time slot of the morning consultation hours. This time was determined by the hospital's schedule.

I called ahead because I was going to be 3-5 minutes late due to traffic, but I was told that "an after-hours fee will be charged if I am late." I replied, "In that case, I will cancel the scheduled time. If you can't accommodate me even by a few minutes, I'll go at a different time..." However, I was told to "check with my supervisor," and although I reiterated that I wouldn't go if it wasn't possible, I was urged to come in "just for today," so I hurried there and arrived about 5 minutes late.

The atmosphere at the reception upon arrival was extremely unpleasant. After paying within a minute or two and turning my back, I overheard an older staff member repeatedly and loudly telling a younger staff member, "Sorry it's so late—you can go on break," making sarcastic remarks about me.

There was the last patient and their dog at the exit, so I wasn't the only one waiting.

Despite having expressed my willingness to come at a different time if even a few minutes were too long, the hospital insisted on my visit, yet directed such dissatisfaction towards me. As a long-time patient, I was deeply shocked.

While I appreciate the doctors' consultations, I have serious doubts about the coordination and customer service among the reception and staff.

My cat suddenly developed blood in her urine around 11 PM, so I took her to the emergency vet.

Upon arrival, I called out to the reception staff several times, but no one came for about 10 minutes. Finally, a receptionist came to assist me. They may have been busy because it was nighttime, but I think it would be reassuring if there was a call button or something similar at the reception, especially in an emergency.

During the examination, she underwent blood tests, urine tests, and an ultrasound. I suspected cystitis, but the vet explained that "there were bacteria in the urine, but no swelling in the urethra," and prescribed only pain medication before sending us home.

However, the next day, I took her to my usual veterinary clinic in Daikanyama, where she was diagnosed with inflammation and pus in the urinary tract between the kidneys and bladder. Since the culture test results would take over a week, the vet prescribed antibiotics based on their experience, and the blood in her urine improved within 2-3 days of starting the medication.

Of course, I don't intend to blame the vet at this clinic, and all the staff were very kind and courteous. However, given the nature of an emergency nighttime clinic, I felt that they could have been more careful in diagnosing and treating feline urinary tract diseases.

The consultation fee for this visit, including blood tests, urine tests, ultrasound, and consultation fees, was approximately 60,000 yen, but I wasn't even given the ultrasound images.

Ultimately, my cat received appropriate treatment at another hospital and improved, but I personally will not be using this clinic again in the future.

I went to a university hospital, but on the way home, I started having difficulty breathing, so I searched and searched for this hospital and finally found one. They treated me right away, and when I tried to take him home, I couldn't, so he was hospitalized. I learned a lot, performed surgery, and received help. My cat had a rare disease. His internal organs were very healthy, but he had a respiratory disease and needed a permanent tracheotomy. Caring for him was extremely difficult, and it was impossible to do at home, so the doctor searched for a solution, performed another surgery, and we were finally able to bring him home. It was 23 days from the time we rushed to the hospital until he was discharged. The doctor and nurses monitored him 24/7. I told them it would be very difficult when he got home, but we would do our best, but on the day he was discharged, he suddenly crossed the Rainbow Bridge. He developed the disease in November of last year, went to a university hospital in Fuchu, and received help. I rushed to this hospital, received help and love, and it was my turn to keep him alive. But when I took my eyes off him for a moment, he passed away. I was more stunned than sad. I still can't accept it.

Anyway, the doctors and nurses are all really nice and do a great job, so I'm truly grateful! Thank you very much.

This is a very trustworthy clinic, and I'm so overwhelmed with joy that the surgery was successful that I wanted to post this review 🌹
First, the nurse quickly checked with the doctor and contacted me immediately, allowing us to receive emergency care! They were very polite on the phone, and I was so grateful for their help in the emergency 💐
It's so worrying when animals can't speak! My usually energetic dog experienced this for the first time when his condition changed. It was his first surgery, and I was able to see his face when the general anesthesia was administered, and the surgery was completed successfully!

We requested a two-day hospital stay, and they were incredibly supportive. They were true professionals 💐
As my dog ​​grows older and progresses, I learned so much from them! Their care filled me with warmth, and as a pet owner, I felt empowered by their support 🌹
My family was also overjoyed!!

Thank you for this wonderful experience. I am so grateful!

We will continue to rely on your services in the future.

Please continue to support us in the future ✨
50 years of experience.

My beloved cat was in a dangerous condition due to diabetes, and every vet had given up on her at the end of the year, but Daktari took her in. Furthermore, they provided appropriate treatment, careful support, and accurate advice, and her diabetes improved remarkably. They are a lifesaver. Thank you so much. If you suspect your pet has diabetes, I highly recommend consulting Daktari.

This is a very reassuring hospital that also handles emergencies late at night. They examine pets in private rooms, so you can rest assured that your pet won't encounter other dogs or cats.

However, there was a period when one of the male veterinarians here was overcharging and performing surgeries poorly.

As of 2026, that doctor has left the hospital.

I brought my cat here for an emergency late at night and I’m truly thankful for their help. The whole team was very kind and professional, and they explained everything clearly in English. It was a very stressful situation for me, but they made me feel supported and took great care of my cat. She is now recovering well thanks to them. I would definitely recommend this hospital!!!

Very nice and compassionate English speaking vet and team. Hospital seemed very clean and modern. We came in without a booking and were seen immediately. They took care of our dog’s minor problem in no time. Appreciate your help so much!!! Arigato 🙏 …

We received emergency care at night.

My family and I went out for dinner, and while we were out, our Maltipoo ate some milk chocolate! I was worried that he might develop acute pancreatitis, so I called even though it was past 9 PM, and the doctor on duty was incredibly kind and helpful. It had been two years since our last visit, but they were so kind. They quickly examined him and performed a gastric lavage to clean his stomach. They also checked on him afterward and gave him medication to stop the nausea. They even prescribed medication for the next day, which was a huge help. Thanks to them, we were able to relax completely. He also has a history of allergies, so they gave us food samples as a preventative measure and explained everything clearly. I am truly grateful.

I've used your emergency services several times at night.

This time, I needed your help with a case of accidental ingestion.

Thank you so much for the prompt and successful treatment.

I also received advice on allergies and other potential causes based on the appearance of the animal, which helped me see a way to deal with the itching that had been bothering me. Thank you very much.

The veterinarians are very kind and warm, and their explanations are easy to understand, so I feel at ease leaving my precious family member with them. The clinic is spacious and clean. Some people say that the medical expenses are high, but they are watching over us 24 hours a day, so although we are by no means wealthy, I don't think that's the case. My pet is sensitive, so he won't eat at the hospital. Thank you so much for showing concern when the doctor said he wouldn't eat, and for wiping his body clean when he was discharged.
I visited urgently in the middle of the night, and they responded very politely and promptly. Thank you very much.

I have been using your services for some time.
I was worried when my cat knocked over an air freshener bottle and started licking the liquid off its body, so I called you at night. I had been away from home during the day and only discovered the incident when I returned home, so even though the information was vague, you handled the situation very courteously.
It is very reassuring to have staff on hand at all times, even at night. I didn't visit the clinic, and only received treatment over the phone, but I would like to thank you for your kind consideration.

Thank you so much for everything.

As a pet owner, I'm so sad that I couldn't be there for my rabbit's final moments, but thanks to the hospital staff who captured a video of her last moments, I feel a little better.

The veterinarians and reception staff were incredibly supportive, and even though it was an emergency, I'm so glad we came here.

Thank you for the flowers too 🌼
I'll display them with my rabbit!

We are the family of Oppo, an 18-year-old cat.

We are deeply grateful to everyone at Daktari Animal Hospital for their care, from emergency night visits to hospitalization, and sadly, for Oppo's passing.

From the emergency examination to bringing him home for his final moments, they explained everything carefully each time and did everything they could.

Above all, the gentle voices and touches on Oppo's face were truly appreciated.

Some posts mention high fees, but I disagree.

If it were 100% human care, it would be expensive too.

It's not an exorbitant amount, and I felt it was a fair price for the careful care they provided, just like for a human.

I am a medical professional with experience working in a general hospital, and I felt that this hospital treated animals just as well as humans during hospitalization.

Because animals cannot communicate through conversation, I believe their care is even more challenging than that for humans.

As a family, we are now grieving the loss of our cat and wondering what we could have done best for him, but I think we would have regretted it even more if we hadn't done anything.

We are grateful that they provided the best possible care, and that we were able to be with him at home until the end. I was also touched when you sent flowers after I informed you of the passing.

I know it's a very demanding job, but please keep up the good work.

A few years ago, my beloved dog was involved in a traffic accident in the middle of the night and was taken in by this hospital. I continued to care for him here until I moved, and the doctors, nurses, and groomers all truly loved my dog. He became very attached to them.

It's true that the fees may be higher than at a regular hospital, but in an emergency, the doctor would wait at the entrance and examine the dog immediately, treating him just like an ambulance would for a human. I remember the director explaining the surgical method to us for several hours.

I now live in a different region, but I think if hospitals like this were commonplace all over the country, dog lovers would be able to live with peace of mind.

Thank you.
I am so grateful.
I was so lucky to see him before he died.
Thank you so much.

I recently had a tooth extracted at another clinic and was worried about the progress, so I called late at night.
You listened to me carefully and explained the medication in a way that was easy to understand, which helped ease my anxiety.
During the phone call, you told me that it wasn't an emergency, so I didn't come in, but I was so grateful for your kind treatment that I decided to write a review.

As other reviewers have mentioned, I was shocked by the high cost.
My dog ​​became ill, and I went there on a referral, only to be told the cost would be over 400,000 yen.
This was an amount I couldn't immediately afford, so I tried to go to another hospital, but they kept making excuses and wouldn't return my dog, asking me how much I was willing to pay, like it was an auction.
A friend called another hospital and inquired about the cost, and it was less than half that, around 100,000 yen.
Not being able to return my dog, being charged such a high price while I was in a state of shock, and then being pressured to write a good review in exchange for a discount—I think they took advantage of me because I'm a woman.
I will never go to this hospital, or the hospital that referred me, again.

I was saved by the accurate emergency testing and diagnosis that was done at night, which revealed the cause of my illness, which I had never even thought of. I am grateful for the kind and thorough care I received afterwards.

In addition to gastrointestinal bleeding of unknown cause, he also had cardiomyopathy and needed a blood transfusion. There were no hospitals in our prefecture that could provide a transfusion, so he was admitted to the hospital on the recommendation of his regular veterinarian. I would like to express my gratitude to the doctors, nurses, and the blood donor Kurobe and his owner for the transfusion. Now, we are finally getting back to normal.

Our relationship began when our previous toy poodle, Momo, became seriously ill and we were introduced to the 24-hour Daktari Animal Hospital.
We visited her every day and she was very kind.
We were also impressed by the thorough and detailed explanations she gave us about her treatment.
Although we were able to send her home temporarily, her condition had progressed so much that we had to say goodbye two weeks later.
She was given cardiac massage with all her might until I asked her to stop. I felt her passion and love, which is something that is not possible just because it is work.
After her journey of 11 and a half years, and her final moments, she was given a lovely grooming and wrapped in a beautiful ribbon and kimono, which truly soothed my heart. Her peaceful expression, as if she had been released from the pain she had just experienced, was such a relief. Thank you so much for delivering flowers as an offering.
---
Even though I know logically that regretting the past is like counting the years of a dead child, various thoughts (like "if only I had done this at that time") ran through my mind.
The thought I felt most at that time was, "If only I had been cared for at Daktari Animal Hospital from the very beginning, when she was a child."
Everyone works in a bright and cheerful atmosphere, and I felt their great teamwork. I believe that is the main reason they create such a comfortable space.
---
Momo-chan was an angel herself, always smiling and loving people. Two months after we said goodbye, we welcomed Hana-chan (who also loves people). This time, we will definitely be caring for her from the very beginning at Daktari Animal Hospital.
The sadness of losing Momo-chan is now turning into twice the joy of living with Momo-chan and Hana-chan.
I am grateful to Daktari Animal Hospital for supporting Hana-chan's life, as she is simply healthy, has lived a long life, and is loved by humans.
I look forward to your continued support.

We were able to help with the final moments of our cat, who had been with us for 10 years.

The cat had a seizure around 4 a.m., so we called without much thought, and they accepted despite their busy schedule.

First of all, thank you to the young male staff member who ran to call the doctor.
I felt that the service was very polite.

And thank you to the doctor and staff on duty that day for performing resuscitation.
You provided accurate guidance and explained the treatment plan.

Thank you to the person who contacted us the next day to report that our cat's condition was worsening.
Thank you, I was able to finish work early.

And also, thank you so much to the doctor who stayed with us and encouraged us until the end.
I was honestly petrified before entering the hospital, but you gave me strength and I was able to be with him until the end.

Thank you for the funeral makeup you applied. I couldn't help but mutter, "So cute..."
It really looked like he was still alive.

The younger cat, who I was worried about how he would react, went into the box once, sniffed it a few times, and then quietly left.
We still don't know if he is aware of his death.

I still feel filled with sadness when I think about it,
but strangely, there is a sense of understanding. Being able to be with him until the very end was a very precious and important thing.

If things had continued as they were, he would have passed away in agony at home, still having seizures, so I would like to express my gratitude once again to everyone who accepted him despite the difficult circumstances of the night and early morning hours.

I think it is a very noble job, and I respect all those who do it.

Thank you.

I've been to many veterinary clinics, but the more I get to know this one, the more unfriendly it seems. Located in Shirokanedai, it's relatively unpopular with pet owners, perhaps because the high fees aren't as common. However, my friendly dog, who used to wag his tail and look happy at other grooming salons, now trembles unbelievably on the way here. Perhaps because he was uncomfortable around the buttocks after being groomed, he started licking his anus, a habit he'd never had before. When I asked, he simply refused. They suggested scaling, which cost 30,000-50,000 yen, including anesthesia, so I assumed it would be around that price, but it ended up costing 150,000 yen. After moving, I asked them to take my dog's epilepsy medication, but they prescribed the wrong dosage (since he's a small dog, the tablets needed to be split, but there were multiple sizes), and he ended up feeling exhausted at home. I thought something was strange, so I read other people's reviews and it seemed to be the case. Hospitals that provide night-time care are rare and I am grateful for them, but in an emergency, if I were to entrust my precious pet to them, I would choose another hospital even if it was a little further away.

Thank you as always.
This is a clinic where the doctor, veterinary nurses, groomers, and all the staff are very kind and attentive when it comes to listening to your concerns.
Thank you so much for your emergency care. It's an amazing hospital. Great doctor. I'm truly grateful.

As someone who works in animal welfare, I regularly visit veterinary clinics in various locations, but this is the worst experience I've ever had, so I'm writing this review.

My senior cat was in very poor health, and it was life-threatening, so I sought a second opinion.

First, I submitted my identification. Although they claim to operate on a strict appointment system, the clinic was practically empty. Nothing began, so I filled out a questionnaire and waited for 30 minutes.

I expressed my concern about my cat's condition, and they said the examination would take two hours. After waiting two hours, they said it would take another two hours.

Four hours for an examination? I couldn't believe it was that bad… I waited, hoping they would examine her thoroughly, but I still hadn't been called. I expressed my concern again and asked to take her home, but as expected, she was so weak I thought she might die.

In the end, the examination didn't seem to warrant four hours, and the explanation from the two young staff members was insufficient and lacked detail.

And the bill came to 140,000 yen.

Did they inflate the price with unnecessary tests? Given the apparent shortage of veterinarians, a regular customer suddenly appeared, and they said it would take another two hours, so my cat was put on the back burner. Even if the original price was that amount, the bill might have been charged four hours later.

They boasted about having top-of-the-line equipment, but my regular vet has invested in better quality equipment (CT scanner). In any case, I felt they only saw animals as tools for making money.

I couldn't build a trusting relationship here; it's far from a place I would entrust my precious pet to.

Afterward, I went to another clinic, and the price was less than one-fifth of what I paid.

More importantly, after explaining the situation, they treated my cat with great care and attention, carefully examining her condition.

I urge pet owners to carefully choose where they entrust their beloved family members.

My cat, thanks to the other clinic, was able to live for about six months.

I hope this will be helpful to others in the future.

My beloved cat, who has since passed away, was a patient at this hospital.

Towards the end of her life, her illness had progressed, and the doctor here suggested euthanasia.

I believe euthanasia is simply human ego. It's absurd to suggest death to an animal that can't speak, an animal whose wishes we can never know.

In reality, my cat desperately wanted to live.

The fact that there was a doctor who suggested euthanasia has always been a source of unease in my heart.

Since the decision to slaughter koalas in Australia (which involved shooting them while calling it euthanasia—what exactly is the concept of euthanasia? If so, would shooting humans also be considered euthanasia?) was reportedly triggered by a veterinarian's opinion, I felt it was important to leave this review.

My cat was diagnosed with diabetes four years ago.
She was drinking a lot of water and seemed unwell, so I took her to the vet. She was admitted to the hospital, but ultimately, it was decided that it would be better to take her home and administer insulin injections there. Before going home, we had a blood glucose monitoring session and insulin injection training.
The training took about two hours.
The nurse (or someone similar) gave us thorough and careful training until we could administer the injections at home with confidence.
Thanks to that, we were able to administer the appropriate amount of insulin injections while consulting with the vet about the blood glucose results, and incredibly, she was in remission within just two weeks of our initial hospital visit.
Even now, we monitor her blood glucose levels occasionally and carefully monitor her diet based on the vet's guidance to maintain her condition.
I'm truly grateful.

I used to go there, but I stopped going when my doctor opened their own practice or moved elsewhere. They were very thorough in their examinations. Looking back now, I think the fees were ridiculously high, but considering they're open 24 hours a day and have all the necessary medical equipment, I suppose it's understandable. It's a good option for those with ample funds or those whose medical condition requires it.
I panicked and called because my dog ​​drank a teacup of chrysanthemum tea with honey in it in the middle of the night. I was relieved when a kind nurse calmly explained everything to me.

I previously used their services for my last cat during its final days (though it's hard to call it "care"...). I hospitalized it for five days, and while some veterinarians are very kind, others are arrogant and unpleasant. The hospital environment was extremely poor. The disinfectant smell in the room was so strong it was suffocating even for a human. The small oxygen chamber where the cat was kept had a hard floor and only a metal tray for it to sleep on. I was shocked and brought a pet blanket from home, but I was appalled that they would leave a weakened cat in such a terrible place. There were also several large dogs hospitalized in the room, constantly barking and growling.

The hospitalization fees were very high, so surely they could have separated the cat and dogs. On the first day of hospitalization, the doctor on duty said, "Let's keep it for five days for now," and the cat passed away exactly five days later. The veterinarian is a professional, and probably knew that five days was the limit, but I thought it was terrible that they didn't tell us anything and instead turned that five-day life into money. If that was the case, couldn't they have at least shown some kindness by letting the animal spend its last days in a slightly better environment? I still regret letting it spend its final days in such a terrible place.

I called at 5am and they were very accommodating. 
I called at 5am to inquire about my kitten's possible fracture, and despite being busy they took the time to carefully interview me. I was very worried, but they told me that based on the condition it was probably not an emergency, so I was able to wait calmly until the clinic opened during the day. Thank you very much.

My dog ​​is always well cared for here. They provide very thorough explanations, meticulous care, and complete examinations. Treatment plans can vary depending on the veterinarian, so it might be a good idea to choose a regular veterinarian and have them see the same one for everything except emergencies. The groomers are also kind and take great care of pets. I recommend having pet health insurance.
Last night, I was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, so I quickly researched hospitals that were open late at night and went to this large hospital closest to my house without hesitation. …

This is the same hospital where my previous cat, who lived to be 20 years and 9 months old, was cared for about 8 years ago.
I had to return here as an emergency patient for the first time in a long time …

My dog, Ketty, was about to lose her front teeth! She was having epileptic seizures! I panicked! I went to Daktari Animal Hospital because that's where I get her prescribed epilepsy medication. I was impressed by the latest medical …

First of all, I haven't been to this clinic. Some of you might think, "Then why write a review?", but I'm writing this because the cost was so high that it was beyond the point of even considering the price I inquired about over the phone. …

I wouldn't even give it one star.

My dog's eye suddenly swelled up and started bleeding, so even though it was …

I cannot accept the fact that there were errors in the examination of my dog, and that they are charging me 50,000 yen despite the promised tests not being performed. When I refused to pay, they tried to force me to pay by holding my dog …
